name: Quick Facedown
description: Two minutes, phone down, no stake. Finish and a sponsor pays a small reward.
steps: Start; your wallet signs in once (no stake)
Lay the phone face-down with FACEDOWN open (the screen goes dark)
When it buzzes, knock on the back (4 checks, one in every 30 s)
Switching apps or missing a check ends the session unverified
why: Most people won't put money at risk on day one (13.7% accepted deposits vs 90% rewards in Halpern et al., NEJM 2015). Free sessions let anyone start; staking is the upgrade.

name: Urge Break
description: Ten minutes face-down instead of the app you were about to open. A sponsor pays a small reward.
steps: Start; your wallet signs in once (no stake)
Lay the phone face-down with FACEDOWN open (the screen goes dark)
When it buzzes, knock on the back (2 checks, one in every 5 minutes)
Switching apps or missing a check ends the session unverified
why: Turns the urge itself into a verified session.

name: Quick Facedown
description: Lock 1 SKR for the session; you get it back whether you finish or not. Finish and a sponsor pays a reward and your streak grows.
steps: Stake and start; your wallet signs once
Lay the phone face-down with FACEDOWN open (the screen goes dark)
When it buzzes, knock on the back (4 checks, one in every 30 s)
Switching apps or missing a check ends the session: stake returned, no reward
why: Nobody loses principal, so it isn't a bet: finishing earns the sponsor reward and keeps the streak. On mainnet the locked stake can earn yield that funds the reward (roadmap).

name: Quick Facedown
description: Two minutes, phone down, one thing in mind. Stake 1 SKR: finish and get it back plus a bonus from the pool. Quit and your stake is locked for a week, not lost.
steps: Stake and start; your wallet signs once
Lay the phone face-down with FACEDOWN open (the screen goes dark)
When it buzzes, knock on the back (4 checks, one in every 30 s)
Switching apps or missing two checks locks the stake for 7 days (14, then 30 if you quit again within a month), then it comes back
why: Focus apps run on a local timer, so nobody can put money on them. PRESENCE times the session on the server, ties it to one Seeker, and checks for a human at unpredictable moments, so a stake can ride on it.
